text: Should I tell the truth about my father's tax fraud, or protect him because he is my father?
rationale: Filial loyalty against truthfulness; both homes are named in the question and both carry positions.

text: My husband confessed an affair and asked me to lie to his family about it.
rationale: Infidelity plus a demanded lie; either topic is a defensible home.

text: Is it right to end a marriage because he drinks himself senseless every night?
rationale: Grounds for divorce and the moral standing of habitual drunkenness.

text: My brother stole from me and now says he is sorry; must I forgive him?
rationale: Theft inside a family and the demand to forgive a repentant offender.

text: Can I refuse to fight in a war I believe is unjust even if the law commands it?
rationale: Conscientious refusal sits equally in war ethics and obedience to the state.

text: Is it worse to spread a true rumour about a colleague or to lie about him?
rationale: Damaging true speech against falsehood; both homes carry positions.

text: My elderly mother is dying and asks me to help her die; what do I owe her?
rationale: Assisted dying requested by the parent one owes care to.

text: Is it wrong to charge my ageing mother interest on a loan I made her?
rationale: Interest-taking inside a family; lending ethics and filial duty both apply.

text: The man who killed my brother went free; would revenge be justified?
rationale: Private vengeance that would itself be a killing.

text: Is the death penalty a kind of killing, or is executing a murderer different?
rationale: Judicial execution measured against the general prohibition on killing.

text: I am furious at the friend who wronged me and cannot decide whether to forgive him.
rationale: Anger at an offender and how the wrong should be answered.

text: Is it stealing to take food from the supermarket bins when I have no money and the rich throw it away?
rationale: Necessity taking and the duties of the wealthy toward the hungry.

text: My houseguest has stayed a month and I am too afraid of a confrontation to ask him to leave.
rationale: Limits of welcome and the nerve required to end it.

text: Is it judgmental to criticise how my mother raised us?
rationale: Judging another's conduct where the other is a parent.

text: I envy my colleague's promotion and I have started spreading rumours about him.
rationale: Envy expressed as damaging speech; both homes are lexically present.

text: My employer wants me to sign a false statement and I am too scared to refuse.
rationale: A demanded falsehood and the courage needed to refuse it.

text: Is it wrong to boast about how much I gave to charity?
rationale: Almsgiving performed for admiration.

text: May I break a promise to my wife in order to care for my mother?
rationale: A promise given against filial care owed; both obligations are named.

text: A friend said he wants to kill himself and made me promise to tell nobody.
rationale: A promised confidence against disclosure that might save a life.

text: Is it wrong to kill a deer for meat when I could buy it from a butcher instead?
rationale: Killing an animal for food; the taking of life is the second home.
